notes.summary: A ratio compares two quantities of the same kind; a proportion says two ratios are equal. This topic also covers partnership (sharing profit) and problems on ages. SSC asks 1 to 2 questions in Tier 1 and 1 to 2 in Tier 2, and the same ratio thinking is used in almost every other arithmetic topic.

concepts.title: What a ratio is
concepts.body:
A ratio compares two quantities of the same kind by division. a : b means a/b. The first term is the antecedent and the second is the consequent.

  • Both quantities must be in the same unit. 50 paise : ₹2 = 50 : 200 = 1 : 4.
  • A ratio does not change if both terms are multiplied or divided by the same number. 12 : 18 = 2 : 3.
  • If a : b = 2 : 3, write a = 2k and b = 3k. This one step solves most questions.
  • To compare two ratios, cross-multiply. Is 3/5 bigger than 4/7? 3 × 7 = 21 and 5 × 4 = 20, so 3/5 is bigger.

concepts.title: Combining ratios
concepts.body:
To join A : B and B : C into A : B : C, make the common term B equal.

Example: A : B = 3 : 4 and B : C = 6 : 7. LCM of 4 and 6 is 12. A : B = 9 : 12 and B : C = 12 : 14, so A : B : C = 9 : 12 : 14.

Quick method for A : B = a : b and B : C = c : d: A : B : C = ac : bc : bd.

  • A : C = (A : B) × (B : C). With the numbers above, A : C = (3 × 6) : (4 × 7) = 18 : 28 = 9 : 14.
  • The compound ratio of a : b and c : d is ac : bd.
  • If 2A = 3B = 4C, then A : B : C = 1/2 : 1/3 : 1/4 = 6 : 4 : 3 (multiply by the LCM 12).

concepts.title: Dividing a quantity in a ratio
concepts.body:
To divide an amount S in the ratio a : b : c, total parts = a + b + c and one part = S ÷ (a + b + c).

Share of A = a/(a + b + c) × S.

  • Divide ₹1,800 in 2 : 3 : 4. One part = 1800/9 = 200. Shares are ₹400, ₹600, ₹800.
  • If a difference is given, divide the difference by the difference in parts. Shares 5 : 3 : 4 and P gets ₹1,500 more than R: 5 − 4 = 1 part = ₹1,500, so Q = 3 × 1500 = ₹4,500.
  • For a fractional ratio like 1/2 : 1/3 : 1/4, multiply every term by the LCM of denominators (12) to get 6 : 4 : 3.
  • If A gets ₹x more after someone else gives ₹y, write the shares as multiples of k and form one equation.

concepts.title: Ratio after a percent change
concepts.body:
If quantities in the ratio a : b change by p% and q%, the new ratio is a(100 + p) : b(100 + q).

Example: salaries are 2 : 3. A gets a 15% rise and B a 10% rise. New ratio = 2 × 115 : 3 × 110 = 230 : 330 = 23 : 33.

Also useful: if A is 20% more than B, A : B = 120 : 100 = 6 : 5. If A is 25% less than B, A : B = 75 : 100 = 3 : 4.

concepts.title: Proportion and the proportionals
concepts.body:
Four numbers a, b, c, d are in proportion (a : b :: c : d) when a/b = c/d, that is a × d = b × c (product of extremes = product of means).

AskedRuleExample
Fourth proportional to a, b, cd = bc/a4, 9, 12: d = 9 × 12/4 = 27
Third proportional to a, bc = b²/a16, 24: c = 576/16 = 36
Mean proportional between a, b√(ab)9, 16: √144 = 12
  • a, b, c are in continued proportion when a : b = b : c, so b² = ac.
  • The third proportional uses the two given numbers in order. The third proportional to 24 and 16 is 16²/24 = 32/3, not 36.

concepts.title: Adding or subtracting the same number
concepts.body:
When the same x is added to (or subtracted from) each term, form the equation and cross-multiply.

Two numbers are 3 : 5. Subtract 9 from each and they become 12 : 23. Write 3k and 5k: (3k − 9)/(5k − 9) = 12/23, so 69k − 207 = 60k − 108, k = 11, numbers 33 and 55.

Shortcut for four numbers: the number x to be added to a, b, c, d so that they are in proportion is x = (bc − ad)/(a + d − b − c). For subtraction use x = (ad − bc)/(a + d − b − c).

Check by putting x back: the new a × d must equal the new b × c.

concepts.title: Componendo, dividendo and other rules
concepts.body:
If a/b = c/d, then:

  • Invertendo: b/a = d/c
  • Alternendo: a/c = b/d
  • Componendo: (a + b)/b = (c + d)/d
  • Dividendo: (a − b)/b = (c − d)/d
  • Componendo and dividendo: (a + b)/(a − b) = (c + d)/(c − d)

It works both ways. If (a + b)/(a − b) = 7/3, then a/b = (7 + 3)/(7 − 3) = 10/4 = 5/2.

For an expression like (6a + 13b)/(6a − 13b) with a/b = 7/6, put a = 7, b = 6: (42 + 78)/(42 − 78) = 120/(−36) = −10/3.

concepts.title: Duplicate, triplicate and variation
concepts.body:
NameOf a : b
Duplicate ratioa² : b²
Sub-duplicate ratio√a : √b
Triplicate ratioa³ : b³
Sub-triplicate ratio∛a : ∛b
Inverse (reciprocal) ratiob : a

Direct variation: y ∝ x means y = kx, so y₁/y₂ = x₁/x₂. Inverse variation: y ∝ 1/x means x₁y₁ = x₂y₂.

When the price of a stone varies as the square of its weight, breaking it always causes a loss. A stone worth P broken in the ratio a : b : c is then worth P × (a² + b² + c²)/(a + b + c)².

concepts.title: Coins and notes
concepts.body:
Be careful to separate the number of coins from their value.

Value ratio = number ratio × face value of each coin.

Example: ₹1, 50 p and 25 p coins are in number ratio 5 : 6 : 8. Value ratio = 5 × 1 : 6 × 0.5 : 8 × 0.25 = 5 : 3 : 2. If the total is ₹210, one value part = ₹21, so 50 p coins are worth ₹63, which is 126 coins.

If the total count is given, split the count first, then multiply each count by its value.

concepts.title: Income, expenditure and savings
concepts.body:
Savings = Income − Expenditure.

Write incomes as 5x, 4x and expenditures as 3y, 2y, then use the savings information to form two equations.

Example: incomes 5 : 4, expenditures 3 : 2, each saves ₹2,000. 5x − 3y = 2000 and 4x − 2y = 2000. Solving gives x = 1000, y = 1000. A’s income = ₹5,000.

When both save the same amount, a quick check: income difference equals expenditure difference.

concepts.title: Partnership: capital and time
concepts.body:
Profit is shared in the ratio of capital × time (called the equivalent capital).

  • Same time for all: profit ratio = capital ratio.
  • Same capital: profit ratio = time ratio.
  • Someone who joins after 4 months in a 12-month year invests for 8 months.
  • To find a time ratio, divide: time ratio = profit ratio ÷ capital ratio, term by term. Capitals 3 : 4 : 8 and profits 2 : 3 : 5 give times 2/3 : 3/4 : 5/8 = 16 : 18 : 15.

A sleeping partner only invests money. A working partner may first take a salary or a percent of profit; only the rest is shared by capital × time.

concepts.title: Partnership: capital changes midway
concepts.body:
Split the year into periods. In each period multiply the capital at that time by the months, then add.

Example: A starts with ₹40,000 and adds ₹10,000 after 3 months. A’s equivalent capital = 40000 × 3 + 50000 × 9 = 5,70,000.

If capital rises by 50% after 4 months from a ratio 2 : 3 : 5, use A = 2 × 4 + 3 × 8 = 32 directly in ratio units; you do not need real amounts.

concepts.title: Ages: the difference never changes
concepts.body:
The difference between two people’s ages stays the same for life. Use this to solve ratio questions fast.

A : B = 5 : 7 now and was 2 : 3 six years ago. Now the difference is 2 parts; earlier the ratio 2 : 3 has difference 1 part. Make the differences equal: 2 : 3 becomes 4 : 6. So 5 parts − 4 parts = 1 part = 6 years. A = 30, B = 42.

Algebra method: (5x − 6)/(7x − 6) = 2/3, so 15x − 18 = 14x − 12, x = 6.

Each year everyone gets 1 year older, so a group of n people gets n years older in total.

concepts.title: Ages: equations and family averages
concepts.body:
• “A is n times as old as B” means A = nB. “n years ago” subtract n from each person; “after n years” add n to each.
  • Sum of ages of a group grows by (number of people × years).
  • Average-age questions: total age = average × number of people. If father and mother average 40 and the three of them average 30, daughter = 90 − 80 = 10.
  • A child born x years ago adds only x years to the total, not the group average times anything.
  • Always check the answer: ages must be positive and fit every condition.

varieties.name: Ratio basics and combining ratios
varieties.how:
1. Make the common term equal using its LCM.
  2. Write the joined ratio.
  3. For a percent change, multiply each term by (100 + change).

example.q: If A : B = 3 : 4 and B : C = 6 : 7, find A : B : C.

varieties.name: Dividing an amount in a ratio
varieties.how:
1. Clear fractions in the ratio using the LCM.
  2. One part = total ÷ sum of parts (or difference ÷ difference of parts).
  3. Multiply by the parts asked for.

example.q: Divide ₹6,500 among P, Q and R in the ratio 1/2 : 1/3 : 1/4. What is Q’s share?

varieties.name: Coins and notes
varieties.how: Turn the number ratio into a value ratio by multiplying each term by the coin’s value. Split the total money in the value ratio, then divide by the coin’s value to get the count.

example.q: A bag has ₹1, 50 paise and 25 paise coins in the ratio 5 : 6 : 8. The total is ₹210. How many 50 paise coins are there?

varieties.name: Mean, third and fourth proportional
varieties.how: Fourth proportional to a, b, c = bc/a. Third proportional to a, b = b²/a. Mean proportional between a, b = √(ab).

example.q: Find the third proportional to 16 and 24.

varieties.name: Adding or subtracting the same number
varieties.how: Write the new terms with x, set product of extremes = product of means and solve. Shortcut for adding: x = (bc − ad)/(a + d − b − c).

example.q: What number must be added to each of 7, 11, 19 and 29 so that they are in proportion?

varieties.name: Income, expenditure and savings
varieties.how: Let incomes be ax and bx and expenditures cy and dy. Savings give two equations; solve for x and y.

example.q: The incomes of A and B are in the ratio 5 : 4 and their expenditures in the ratio 3 : 2. Each saves ₹2,000. Find A’s income.

varieties.name: Componendo-dividendo and ratio expressions
varieties.how: If (a + b)/(a − b) = m/n, then a/b = (m + n)/(m − n). For an expression in a and b, put a and b equal to the ratio values.

example.q: If (a + b)/(a − b) = 7/3, find a : b.

varieties.name: Squares, cubes and variation
varieties.how: Write the varying quantity as k × (weight)² (or cube, or 1/x). Compare values using squared parts.

example.q: The price of a diamond varies as the square of its weight. A diamond worth ₹36,000 breaks into three pieces with weights in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3. Find the loss.

varieties.name: Partnership
varieties.how: Multiply each capital by its months. Split the profit in that ratio.

example.q: A starts a business with ₹24,000. B joins after 4 months with ₹36,000 and C after 6 months with ₹30,000. The year’s profit is ₹42,000. Find C’s share.

varieties.name: Partnership with changing capital
varieties.how: Break each partner’s year into periods with a fixed capital. Add capital × months over the periods, then split the profit.

example.q: A and B start with ₹40,000 and ₹60,000. After 3 months A adds ₹10,000 and B withdraws ₹15,000. The year’s profit is ₹15,400. Find B’s share.

varieties.name: Ages in ratio now and later
varieties.how: Write ages as multiples of x, shift both by the same years and equate to the new ratio. Or use the fact that the age difference is constant.

example.q: The ages of A and B are in the ratio 5 : 7. Six years ago the ratio was 2 : 3. What is B’s present age?

varieties.name: Age puzzles with sums, multiples and averages
varieties.how: Use one letter for one person, write every sentence as an equation, and shift every person by the same years.

example.q: The sum of the ages of a father and his son is 50 years. Five years ago the father was 7 times as old as the son. Find the father’s present age.

tips: Turn every ratio into multiples of one letter: a : b = 2 : 3 means a = 2k, b = 3k.
In options-based questions, the answer must be a multiple of the right part. If shares are 5 : 3 and the total is 64, each share is a multiple of 8.
Fractional ratios: multiply every term by the LCM of the denominators first.
In age questions, use the constant difference: make the differences of the two ratios equal and compare parts.
Partnership is always capital × time. Count months carefully when someone joins late or leaves early.
For four numbers in proportion, check the options by testing a × d = b × c rather than solving.
traps: The third proportional to a and b is b²/a, and the order matters.
Coins: the ratio of numbers is not the ratio of values. Multiply by the face value first.
If a person joins after 4 months, they invest for 8 months, not 4.
“n years ago” means subtract n from every person’s age, not just one.

questions.q: Divide ₹ 1,250 between A and B in the ratio 2 : 3. What is B’s share?
What is the mean proportional between 9 and 16?
If A : B = 2 : 3 and B : C = 4 : 5, then A : B : C is:
What is the fourth proportional to 4, 9 and 12?
A and B start a business with ₹ 30,000 and ₹ 45,000. After 4 months, C joins with ₹ 60,000. Out of a total annual profit of ₹ 23,000, what is C’s share?
Two numbers are in the ratio 3 : 5. If 9 is subtracted from each, the new numbers are in the ratio 12 : 23. What is the smaller number?
questions.solution:
Let the numbers be 3x and 5x.
(3x − 9)/(5x − 9) = 12/23 → 69x − 207 = 60x − 108.
9x = 99 → x = 11. Smaller number = 33.
